title: 2009 AMC 8 Problem 8
statement: The length of a rectangle is increased by \(10\%\) and the width is decreased by \(10\%.\) What percent of the old area is the new area?

solutions.text:
Let the old length and width be \(l\) and \(w,\) so the old area is \(lw.\)

The new length is \(1.1l,\) and the new width is \(0.9w.\) Thus the new area is \(1.1\cdot0.9lw=0.99lw.\)

This shows that the new area is \(99\%\) of the old area.

Thus, B is the correct answer.
hints: Multiply the scale factors for length and width.
The new area is \(1.10\cdot0.90\) times the old area.
